newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SKINNER TIES COURSE RECORD WITH 62 FOR BUICK OPEN LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SKINNER TIES COURSE RECORD WITH 62 FOR BUICK OPEN LEAD.

text.p: Sonny Skinner, who has never finished higher than 13th in a PGA Tour event, tied the course record with a 10-under-par 62 Thursday to seize the first-round lead at the $1.5 million Buick Open.
Skinner, 202nd on the money list, led Nolan Henke by four shots and a group of 10 golfers, including Vijay Singh and Lanny Wadkins, by three.

Skinner started on the back nine and birdied five of the first eight holes. He was even hotter on the back nine with birdies on his last four holes to tie Jim Furyk's course record, set in 1995. Furyk is among the group at 5-under.

After beginning his round with a par on 10, Skinner ran off three straight birdies. The first two came when he sank putts of 16 and 20 feet. He parred 14 and 15 but remained hot with his putter, rolling in birdies of 18 feet on 16 and 40 feet on 17.
Skinner managed just one birdie over the next six holes but used strong iron play to post birdies on six through nine. In all, he needed just 23 putts to complete his round.

"I woke up like I always do," said Skinner, who has missed nine of 14 cuts this season. "I've been playing and thinking well. It hasn't always been that way. It's amazing how playing well affects your energy level.
Henke also began on the back nine and muddled through the first six holes with two birdies and two bogeys. But he righted himself after that, posting six birdies without a bogey.
"I didn't hit the ball that well," said Henke. "I missed a few fairways. I've got some work to do on my ball-striking. My putter got me out of a lot of trouble."

Tiger Woods, the Tour's leading money winner, carded a 72 to stand 10 shots off the pace. Woods, whose four victories include the Masters, has seven top-10 finishes but is in danger of missing the cut for the first time in 24 professional events.

Defending champion and British Open winner Justin Leonard, who won his first Tour event here last year, carded a 2-under 70. Leonard's $1,090,275 in earnings is third high in the PGA this year, trailing only Woods and Australia's Steve Elkington, who also shot 70 in his first round here.
The par-72 Warwick Hills Golf and Country Club course measures 7,105 yards.
